name: Greenlam Industries Ltd
tagline: India's largest laminates & decorative-surfaces maker, mid-cap, diversifying into plywood and particle board on heavy capex - a solid franchise but not an aggressive-multibagger fit
business_overview: Greenlam (demerged from Greenply in 2013) is India's largest manufacturer of decorative laminates, with a strong export franchise, plus veneers, engineered wood flooring and doors. It has recently entered plywood (Allied) and particle board / chipboard, funded by a large multi-year capex programme. FY26 consolidated revenue crossed Rs 3,000 Cr for the first time (~Rs 3,046 Cr).
fundamentals_table: ~13.5% Q4FY26 (recovered from ~5.6% a year earlier as new capacity ramps)
FY26 revenue ~Rs 3,046 Cr; Q4FY26 +25.8% YoY; management/analyst guide ~13% consolidated revenue CAGR FY26-28E
Net debt/EBITDA ~3.2x FY26 (elevated), guided down to ~1.9x by FY28E as capex intensity falls
fundamentals_narrative: Laminates & Allied (the core, ~two-thirds of revenue) is healthy - FY26 segment revenue +14.4% YoY with EBITDA margin up ~350 bps to ~17.2%. The newer legs are a drag today: Plywood & Allied is still EBITDA-negative (~-3.2%) and the chipboard plant is only ramping. Returns are depressed by the capex bulge and elevated leverage (net debt/EBITDA ~3.2x), both expected to improve into FY28 if the new capacities ramp on plan. This is a genuine sector leader with pricing power in laminates, but growth is guided to low-teens and the balance sheet needs a couple of years to normalise.

bull_case: Clear #1 position in Indian decorative laminates with a real export franchise and improving core-segment margins (~17% EBITDA, +350 bps YoY)
Capex cycle largely done - operating leverage and de-leveraging (net debt/EBITDA 3.2x -> ~1.9x guided) could lift reported returns into FY28
New plywood and particle-board segments add TAM if they turn profitable on ramp
bear_case: External lead is an implied guidance MISS - @Aditya_joshi12 used Greenlam as a distractor in a quiz whose answer (a company that beat FY25 guidance) was Sonu Infratech, not Greenlam - and no view was stated
Returns still weak (3yr ROE ~7.9%) and leverage elevated; the improvement is a forward expectation, not yet delivered
Plywood segment EBITDA-negative; particle board is a competitive, cyclical, commoditised category dominated by incumbents
~13% revenue CAGR guidance is nowhere near a 10x-in-2-3-years or 100x-in-10-years trajectory, and at a ~Rs 6,455 Cr market cap the size math already works against an aggressive thesis
verdict_headline: A good-quality laminates leader in a capex-digestion phase - worth watching for the FY28 de-leveraging/return-normalisation, but the growth rate and size do not fit this screen's aggressive framework
